+# Iteration 0.013 · n = 7 of 99 · 2026-09-24 · author: twelve lenses · round 7
+
+## Twelve lenses
+
+### Aset
+SSSES (business case): security 86 · stability 74 · scalability 72 · efficiency 70 · succinctness 66
+
+Founder, investors, customers: I read the deck a seventh time for echoes across segments. Round six worked one event, in EDU, and stated when it withdraws. Round seven works a second, in FOOD, on its own clock — material fact to approved enterprise severity — against the same single-customer baseline the model declares, held to the same null and stop rule. I checked the two specimens reinforce rather than compete: one number, two clocks, each re-derived when the inputs move. The register grows to fifteen decisions, and both carriers on S2 and S18 say so. Consistency is the truth I guard, and this round it reaches across the segments, not one.

+### Asar
+SSSES (business case): security 85 · stability 74 · scalability 72 · efficiency 70 · succinctness 65
+
+Read whole, the deck now says its method is not a single lucky example. Round five gave one event; round seven gives a second on a different clock, and both reconcile to the same declared baseline — the single customer applied to FOOD's material-fact-to-severity sequence, never a second number. For investors, that is the difference between an anecdote and a method that repeats. For customers, it means the way your value is measured does not change with your segment; only your clock does. The synthesis: a business case that works one specimen persuades once; a case that works the same specimen twice, on two clocks, shows the instrument, not the outcome.
